walkthroughs.body_html:
Living Under Nazi Rule 1933-1945 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Living Under Nazi Rule 1933-1945 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Living Under Nazi Rule 1933-1945.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which Article of Versailles forced Germany to accept war guilt?
options: Article 48
Article 231
Article 14
Article 5

mcqs.q: What ended the period of Weimar stability?
options: Munich Putsch
Reichstag Fire
Wall Street Crash 1929
Hyperinflation

mcqs.q: How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.
Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.

mcqs.q: What was the political significance of the Reichstag Fire?
options: The fire destroyed all of Berlin and forced people to support the Nazis.
Hitler personally set the fire and blamed it on the Communists.
Hitler used it to issue the Reichstag Fire Decree suspending civil liberties, jail Communists, and create the conditions for the Enabling Act of March 1933.
It began when the USSR shot down a US spy plane.
